explanation: Abundant means more than enough — plentiful. Tip: 'abound' = to be full of. 'Scarce' is the opposite trap.
Reluctant means not wanting to do something — unwilling. 'Eager' is the opposite trap.
Vivid means bright and strong, like vivid colors. Root 'viv' = life (vivid things look alive). 'Dull' is the opposite trap.
Tranquil means peaceful and calm, like a still lake. 'Noisy' is the opposite trap.
Timid means shy and easily scared. Tip: timid sounds like 'timorous' — full of fear. 'Bold' is the opposite trap.
Feeble means weak, without much strength. 'Strong' is the opposite trap.
Vague means not clear or not specific. 'Precise' is the opposite trap.
A novice is a beginner. Root 'nov' = new (like 'novel' and 'renovate'). 'Story' is a trap because 'novel' looks similar, and 'expert' is the opposite.
Ample means enough or more than enough. 'Sample' only looks similar, and 'lacking' is the opposite.
Hostile means unfriendly, like an enemy. Tip: 'hostile' and 'hospital' look alike but are unrelated, and 'welcoming' is the opposite trap.
Elated means extremely happy. 'Delayed' is a trap because 'elated' contains 'late', and 'gloomy' is the opposite.
Rigid means stiff and not able to bend. 'Flexible' is the opposite trap.
Fragile means easily broken. Root 'frag' = break (like 'fragment'). 'Sturdy' is the opposite trap.
Drowsy means sleepy. 'Wet' is a trap because 'drowsy' sounds like 'drown', and 'alert' is the opposite.
Fatigue means extreme tiredness. 'Boredom' is tempting because bored people can seem tired, but boredom is a lack of interest, not a lack of energy.
Peril means serious danger. Tip: 'perilous' = dangerous. 'Journey' is a trap because people face peril on adventures, but they are not the same thing.
Conceal means to hide. 'Reveal' is the opposite trap.
Vacant means empty, with no one using it. Root 'vac' = empty (like 'vacuum' and 'vacation'). 'Occupied' is the opposite trap.
Hasty means done too quickly. Tip: 'haste' = speed. 'Careful' is the opposite trap.
Glum means sad and gloomy. 'Sticky' is a trap because 'glum' sounds like 'glue', and 'cheerful' is the opposite.
Candid means honest and direct — frank. 'Sweet' is a trap because 'candid' looks like 'candy', and 'secretive' is the opposite.
Meager means too small in amount — scanty, like a meager lunch. 'Eager' only looks similar, and 'lavish' is the opposite.
Prudent means wise and careful — sensible. 'Proud' only sounds similar, and 'reckless' is the opposite.
Diligent means hardworking and steady. 'Delicate' only sounds similar, and 'lazy' is the opposite.
Frugal means careful not to waste money — thrifty. 'Wasteful' is the opposite trap.
Concise means saying a lot in few words — brief. 'Wordy' is the opposite trap.
Obsolete means no longer used — outdated, like a flip phone. 'Stubborn' is a trap because 'obstinate' looks similar, and 'modern' is the opposite.
Lenient means not strict — going easy on someone, like a lenient teacher. 'Slanted' is a trap because 'lenient' looks like 'leaning', and 'strict' is the opposite.
Benevolent means kind and wanting to do good. Root 'bene' = good (like 'benefit'). 'Wealthy' is a trap because rich people can give, but being rich is not the same as being kind.
Resilient means able to bounce back after trouble. 'Stubborn' is tempting, but stubborn means refusing to change, not recovering.
Ominous means seeming to warn that something bad will happen. Tip: an 'omen' is a sign. 'Enormous' only rhymes, and 'hopeful' is the opposite.
Tedious means long, dull, and tiring. 'Tidy' only sounds similar, and 'exciting' is the opposite.
Impartial means not taking sides — fair, like a good referee. 'Incomplete' is a trap because 'partial' can mean 'part of', but here it means 'favoring one side'.
Scrutinize means to look at something very closely — examine. 'Ignore' is the opposite trap.
Eloquent means speaking clearly and powerfully. Root 'loq' = speak (like 'loquacious'). 'Loud' is tempting, but volume is not skill.
An adversary is an enemy or opponent. Tip: 'adversity' = hard times. 'Ally' is the opposite trap.
Jovial means cheerful and jolly. 'Youthful' is a trap because 'jovial' looks a bit like 'juvenile', and 'grumpy' is the opposite.
Ponder means to think about something carefully. 'Wander' is a trap because it rhymes, and 'ignore' is the opposite.
Hinder means to get in the way of — obstruct. 'Follow' is a trap because 'hind' means behind, and 'assist' is the opposite.
Vigilant means carefully watching for danger. Tip: a 'vigil' is staying awake to keep watch. 'Brave' is tempting because guards are brave, but being alert is not the same as being brave.
Mediocre means only average, not very good. 'Medical' only looks similar, and 'excellent' is the opposite.
Imminent means about to happen very soon, like an imminent storm. 'Famous' is a trap because 'eminent' (well-known) looks almost the same.
Ambiguous means it could be understood in more than one way. Root 'ambi' = both (like 'ambidextrous'). 'Ambitious' only looks similar, and 'obvious' is the opposite.
Benign means harmless or gentle. Root 'ben' = good (like 'benefit'). 'Dangerous' is the opposite trap.
Garrulous means talking too much, especially about small things. 'Grumpy' is a trap because 'garrulous' sounds growly, but it is about talking, not mood.
Ephemeral means lasting a very short time, like a soap bubble. 'Eternal' is the opposite trap.
Lethargic means slow and without energy — sluggish. 'Deadly' is a trap because 'lethal' looks similar, and 'energetic' is the opposite.
Magnanimous means generous and forgiving, especially toward a rival. 'Huge' is a trap: 'magn' = great (like 'magnify'), but here it means a great spirit, not great size.
Tenacious means holding on and not giving up — persistent. Root 'ten' = hold. 'Yielding' is the opposite trap.
Placate means to calm someone down — soothe. Tip: think 'placid' = calm. 'Provoke' is the opposite trap.
Austere means strict, serious, and plain — stern, like an austere principal. 'Lavish' (fancy and rich) is the opposite of austere's plain side.
Deference means showing respect by going along with someone, like deference to a judge. 'Difference' only looks similar, and 'disrespect' is the opposite.
Meticulous means paying close attention to every detail. 'Fearful' is tempting because careful people can seem cautious, but meticulous is about detail, not fear.
Pragmatic means focused on what actually works — practical. 'Dramatic' only rhymes, and 'idealistic' (focused on dreams) is the opposite.
Ubiquitous means seeming to be everywhere at once, like phones. 'Rare' and 'unique' are opposite traps.
Ancient means very old, so the opposite is modern. 'Old' is the synonym trap.
Generous means happy to give, so the opposite is stingy. 'Kind' is the synonym trap.
Expand means to get bigger, so the opposite is shrink. 'Grow' is the synonym trap.
Victory means a win, so the opposite is defeat. 'Triumph' is the synonym trap.
Permanent means lasting forever, so the opposite is temporary. 'Lasting' is the synonym trap.
Humble means not bragging, so the opposite is arrogant (thinking you're better than others). 'Modest' is the synonym trap.
Reckless means not thinking about danger, so the opposite is careful. 'Careless' is the synonym trap — it looks like 'careful' but means the same as reckless.
Brave means not afraid, so the opposite is cowardly. 'Bold' is the synonym trap.
Ascend means to go up, so the opposite is descend (go down). 'Climb' is the synonym trap.
Inferior means lower in quality or rank, so the opposite is superior. 'Interior' only looks similar, and 'lower' is the synonym trap.
Maximum means the most possible, so the opposite is minimum (the least). Root 'max' = greatest, 'min' = least. 'Most' is the synonym trap.
Graceful means moving smoothly, so the opposite is clumsy. 'Grateful' only looks similar, and 'elegant' is the synonym trap.
Sincere means truly meaning what you say, so the opposite is phony (fake). 'Honest' is the synonym trap.
Exterior means the outside, so the opposite is interior (the inside). Root 'ex' = out. 'Outside' is the synonym trap.
An ally is someone on your side, so the opposite is an enemy. 'Friend' and 'partner' are synonym traps.
Include means to let in, so the opposite is exclude (keep out). 'Contain' is the synonym trap, and 'conclude' only looks similar.
Fertile land grows lots of plants, so the opposite is barren (nothing grows). 'Fruitful' is the synonym trap.
Praise means to say good things about someone, so the opposite is criticize. 'Compliment' is the synonym trap.
Accept means to take or agree to, so the opposite is reject. 'Except' and 'expect' only look similar, and 'receive' is the synonym trap.
Sturdy means strong and solid, so the opposite is flimsy (weak and easily broken). 'Strong' is the synonym trap.
Affluent means rich, so the opposite is poor. 'Fluent' only looks similar, and 'wealthy' is the synonym trap.
Eager means really wanting to do something, so the opposite is uninterested. 'Keen' is the synonym trap.
A veteran is someone with lots of experience, so the opposite is a beginner. 'Soldier' is tempting because veterans are often ex-soldiers, and 'expert' is the synonym trap.
Harsh means rough or cruel, so the opposite is gentle. 'Severe', 'rough', and 'bitter' are synonym traps.
Flexible means able to bend, so the opposite is rigid (stiff). Root 'flex' = bend. 'Bendable' is the synonym trap.
Despair means losing all hope, so the opposite is hope. Tip: 'de' = away from, 'spair' comes from 'hope'. 'Misery' is the synonym trap.
Extravagant means spending way too much, so the opposite is economical (careful with money). 'Lavish' is the synonym trap.
Deliberate means done on purpose, so the opposite is accidental. 'Intentional' is the synonym trap.
Optimistic means expecting good things, so the opposite is pessimistic (expecting bad things). 'Hopeful' is the synonym trap, and 'optical' only looks similar.
Turbulent means wild and stormy, like turbulence on a plane, so the opposite is calm. 'Stormy' is the synonym trap.
Dull can mean boring, dim, or not smart, so the opposite here is brilliant (bright or very smart). 'Boring' and 'dim' are synonym traps.
Vigorous means strong and full of energy, so the opposite is weak. 'Rigorous' only rhymes, and 'energetic' is the synonym trap.
Courteous means polite, so the opposite is rude. 'Courageous' only looks similar, and 'polite' is the synonym trap.
Prohibit means to forbid, so the opposite is allow. 'Forbid' is the synonym trap.
An amateur does something for fun, not for pay, so the opposite is a professional. 'Beginner' is the synonym trap.
Evasive means dodging a question, so the opposite is direct. Tip: evasive comes from 'evade'. 'Avoiding' is the synonym trap, and 'invasive' only looks similar.
Cordial means warm and friendly, so the opposite is unfriendly. Root 'cord' = heart. 'Warm' is the synonym trap, and 'musical' is a trap because of 'chord'.
Explicit means stated clearly and directly, so the opposite is implied (hinted at, not said). 'Clear' is the synonym trap.
Sufficient means enough, so the opposite is inadequate (not enough). 'Enough' is the synonym trap, and 'efficient' only rhymes.
Superb means excellent, so the opposite is awful. 'Excellent' is the synonym trap.
Morose means sullen and gloomy, so the opposite is cheerful. 'Gloomy' is the synonym trap.
Inevitable means certain to happen, so the opposite is avoidable. 'Unavoidable' is the synonym trap, and 'invisible' only looks similar.
Verbose means using too many words, so the opposite is brief. Root 'verb' = word. 'Wordy' is the synonym trap; 'verbal' just means 'in words', not too many.
Belligerent means eager to fight, so the opposite is peaceful. Root 'bell' = war (like 'rebellion'). 'Warlike' is the synonym trap, and 'beautiful' only starts the same way.
Perpetual means lasting forever, so the opposite is fleeting (passing quickly). 'Endless' is the synonym trap.
Taciturn means not saying much, so the opposite is talkative. Tip: 'tacit' = unspoken. 'Quiet' is the synonym trap, and 'tactful' only looks similar.
Exacerbate means to make a problem worse, so the opposite is relieve (make it better). 'Worsen' is the synonym trap, and 'exaggerate' only looks similar.
Opulent means rich and fancy, like a palace, so the opposite is shabby (worn and run-down). 'Luxurious' is the synonym trap.
Negligent means failing to take proper care, so the opposite is attentive. Tip: think 'neglect'. 'Careless' is the synonym trap.
Apathetic means not caring at all, so the opposite is concerned. Root 'a' = without, 'path' = feeling. 'Indifferent' is the synonym trap, and 'pathetic' only looks similar.
Docile means calm and easy to control, like a docile puppy, so the opposite is unruly (wild, hard to control). 'Obedient' is the synonym trap.
Aloof means cool and distant toward others, so the opposite is friendly. 'Distant' is the synonym trap, and 'aloft' (up in the air) only looks similar.
Frivolous means silly and not important, so the opposite is serious. 'Silly' is the synonym trap.
Obstinate means stubborn, refusing to change your mind, so the opposite is agreeable (willing to go along). 'Stubborn' is the synonym trap.
Zealous means full of energy and passion for a cause, so the opposite is unenthusiastic. 'Passionate' is the synonym trap, and 'jealous' only rhymes.
